change_method: Every change is dated and read against a control group: the page's own clicks before and after, divided by what the site's OTHER pages did over the same two periods. The expected figure is modelled from that control group, not measured, and the 95% range carries the control group's own sampling error. A Google update inside the window moves the control group too — that is what the control group is for. A control group narrows the alternatives; it never proves a cause. Each change is dated and read against a control group: the same page's average Google position before and after, minus what the site's OTHER pages did over the same weeks. That removes the part of the move that was the season, the market or a Google update. "Likely helped" means the page beat its control group by more than twice the spread of the control group itself and nothing else changed on that page in the same four weeks; "possibly helped" means it beat the control group by less than that; "no clear effect yet" means it did not. A control group narrows the alternatives: it is never proof of cause.
